maria: Quick Q — noticed a weird duplicate dependency error when bundling the Node TS SDK for Next edge. Happens only in prod build, not dev. Anyone seen this? :thinking:

kevin: Hmm, can you paste the build error and your package.json exports/exports map?

maria: Error snippet: `Error: Multiple competing resolutions found for 'node-fetch'` during next build. Using our SDK installed from npm (redwood-inference-sdk). package.json has "type": "module" and we import with `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference-sdk'`.

samir: That usually means the bundle pulled both CJS and ESM entrypoints from different deps. Next's edge runtime + Vite/webpack can sometimes resolve both. Do you have any duplicate versions in yarn.lock?

maria: lockfile looks single version. Repro steps: `npx create-next-app`, add SDK, set `experimental.edge` routes, build with `next build`. Works locally but on CI (vercel) the production build fails.

kevin: Two things to try fast: 1) Force the SDK to use the ESM entrypoint via alias in next.config.js, 2) ensure `resolve.fullySpecified: false` isn't needed for your bundler. Example alias for Next (webpack):
```js
// next.config.js
module.exports = {
  webpack: (config) => {
    config.resolve.alias['redwood-inference-sdk'] = require.resolve('redwood-inference-sdk/dist/esm/index.js')
    return config
  }
}
```

julia: If you're on Vercel edge, also check the platform's Node version and polyfills. Some packages fall back to `node-fetch` CJS. We published an ESM-only build under `dist/esm` — try importing directly as a temporary repro: `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference-sdk/dist/esm'`

maria: Tried that, still got a warning but build passed on local when I forced import path. CI still fails with duplicate resolution from a transitive (auth-client) that requires `node-fetch` CJS.

samir: For transitive CJS ESM duet, one pattern: use `next-transpile-modules` to force consistent resolution, or add a resolution override in package.json to dedupe to the ESM-friendly version. Example: `resolutions: { 'node-fetch': '3.3.0' }` (yarn).

kevin: Also check package exports field — our SDK has both `exports` for `.` -> `./dist/cjs/index.js` and `./dist/esm/index.js`. Old bundlers may read both. If you can, try adding `package.browser` shim to prefer ESM in the bundle, or set `conditions: ['import']` in a custom resolver.

maria: Good tips. Another wrinkle: streaming responses (ReadableStream) in edge route throwing `TypeError: can't mix stream types` when I enable streaming in SDK. Works in Node serverless but fails in edge.

julia: Edge runtimes expect Web Streams. Our SDK has a `web-streams` polyfill for Node; if you enable streaming in edge, the SDK should avoid Node-only stream APIs. Are you using the `stream: true` option?

maria: Yes `client.chat.stream({ ... })`. Locally with `next dev` it's fine. On edge build it fails during SSR when hydration calls the same helper.

samir: Might be bundling different helper versions into server and edge bundles. Try marking the SDK as external for serverless edge functions in next.config (so platform provides the runtime) or ensure the bundle resolves the `web` condition.

kevin: Quick checklist: 
- confirm `exports` resolution (import vs require)
- try explicit ESM import path as a repro
- dedupe transitive `node-fetch` with resolutions or alias
- for streaming, prefer Web Streams polyfill and ensure it isn't duplicated

maria: Thanks. I'll try alias + resolutions. If CI still fails I'll open a minimal repro repo.

ci-bot: build/pipeline #482 failed on production build (edge). Logs uploaded: https://ci.example.com/builds/482/logs

kevin: Ping me after you open the repro and I'll take a look. Also we should add a short doc in SDK README about bundler caveats for Next/Vite/Edge.

maria: Will do, adding a bullet list and recommended next.config snippets. :+1:

julia: If you want, I can push a tiny patch to prefer ESM exports and add a top-level `exports.import` condition to reduce ambiguity.

maria: That would be awesome. Thanks everyone!
